items.summary: Deserialization of untrusted data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint. The issue is being actively exploited; upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later.
items.plain: Apache Roller lets anyone send a crafted request and run code on the blog server — upgrade to version 6.1.6 or later now.

items.summary: Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in end-of-life Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation and remote code execution, and has been exploited against products bundling Axis such as Confluence Data Center. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on November 18; no fixed 1.x release will be published, so migrate to a maintained SOAP engine.
items.plain: Apache Axis lets attackers run code on servers without logging in and is already being exploited — remove or replace this old software now.

items.summary: An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in REDCap's survey passthrough routing and Data Import processing lets an attacker who knows a valid public survey hash execute arbitrary code on the server. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on November 18 after active exploitation; upgrade to 16.0.49, 17.3.10 or 17.4.4.
items.plain: REDCap lets anyone with a public survey link run code on the research server — upgrade to a fixed release today.
items.product: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap)

items.summary: An improper authorization vulnerability in FortiManager's FGFM service may allow an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the FGFM port to execute code or commands via crafted FGFM packets, before the registration password is verified. Fortinet published fixes on November 10 in advisory FG-IR-26-275; NVD records a CVSS base score of 9.8.
items.plain: FortiManager lets anyone who can reach its device-management port run commands without a password — upgrade to a fixed release now.

items.summary: Deserialization of untrusted data in Puppet's report-processing code, as used by Puppet Server, allows a client holding any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on November 17; Perforce fixed it on November 3 in Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 and 2023.8.13.
items.plain: Puppet Enterprise lets a managed device take over the central management server — upgrade to a fixed release before December 1.
